# 1. How to use this document

This R Markdown is a **drop‑in template** to profile and document your Victoria Police search dataset.
It is designed to be **defensive**—plots and tables render only if the required columns exist.

- Point `data_path` to your Excel/CSV file **or** assign a data frame to `dat` before knitting.
- The **Data Dictionary** pulls column names and types automatically; you can add human‑readable descriptions in the editable table at the end.

```{r libraries}
# Core
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(forcats)

# I/O & utilities
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(skimr)

# Tables
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
```



```{r load-data}
df <-readRDS("../VicPol Search Data Clean/VicPol Search Data Clean.RDS")
```

# 2. Quick structure and quality checks

```{r structure}
glimpse(df)
```

```{r skim}
skimr::skim(df)
```

## 2.1 Basic row completeness

```{r completeness}
df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(!is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "non_missing") %>%
  mutate(total_rows = nrow(df),
         pct_non_missing = non_missing / total_rows) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_non_missing)) %>%
  head(30) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Top 30 columns by completeness") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

# 3. Suggested canonical variables (auto-detected if present)

This section standardises a few common fields used in the search dataset. If your column names differ, update the `coalesce` lines below.

```{r canonical-vars}
# Try to coalesce likely variants into canonical columns
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # Age
    age = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("age", "age_years"), names(df)))),
    # Date/time
    date = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("date", "created", "search_date"), names(df)))),
    # Hit / Found indicator
    found = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("found", "found_flag", "found_drugs", "hit"), names(df)))),
    # Racial appearance
    racial_appearance = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("racial_appearance_transformed", "racial_appearance", "appearance"), names(df)))),
    # Area / Division / Station
    division = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("division", "police_division"), names(df)))),
    station = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("station_uniform", "station", "police_station"), names(df)))),
    # Search type
    search_type = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("search_type___drugs", "search_type_drugs", "search_type"), names(df)))),
    # Contact type
    contact_type = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("contact_type"), names(df)))),
    # LGA
    lga = coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("lga"), names(df))))
  )
```

## 3.1 Derived fields

```{r derived-vars}
# Age group (defensive)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      is.na(age) ~ "Missing",
      age >= 0  & age <= 18 ~ "0 to 18",
      age >= 19 & age <= 25 ~ "19 to 25",
      age >= 26 & age <= 35 ~ "26 to 35",
      age >= 36 & age <= 45 ~ "36 to 45",
      age >= 46 ~ "46 and over",
      TRUE ~ "Missing"
    ),
    age_group = factor(age_group,
      levels = c("0 to 18", "19 to 25", "26 to 35", "36 to 45", "46 and over", "Missing")
    ),
    # Normalise found to Yes/No if it's logical/0-1
    found_norm = case_when(
      is.logical(found) & !is.na(found) ~ if_else(found, "Yes", "No"),
      is.numeric(found) & !is.na(found) ~ if_else(found > 0, "Yes", "No"),
      TRUE ~ as.character(found)
    )
  )
```

# 4. Overview charts (rendered only if columns exist)

## 4.1 Counts by year

```{r by-year, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
if (has_cols(df, date)) {
  df %>%
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(date)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
    count(year) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = n)) +
    geom_col() +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Searches", title = "Search counts by year")
}
```

## 4.2 Age group distribution

```{r age-dist, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
if (has_cols(df, age_group)) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(age_group)) %>%
    count(age_group) %>%
    mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(age_group, p)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Age group", y = "Percent", title = "Age group distribution")
}
```

## 4.3 Hit rate by age group

```{r hit-by-age, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
if (has_cols(df, age_group, found_norm)) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(age_group), !is.na(found_norm)) %>%
    count(age_group, found_norm) %>%
    group_by(age_group) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    ggplot(aes(age_group, prop, fill = found_norm)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Age group", y = "Proportion", fill = "Found", title = "Proportion found by age group")
}
```

## 4.4 Hit rate by racial appearance (if available)

```{r hit-by-race, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
if (has_cols(df, racial_appearance, found_norm)) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(racial_appearance), !is.na(found_norm)) %>%
    mutate(racial_appearance = fct_lump_n(as.factor(racial_appearance), n = 8)) %>%
    count(racial_appearance, found_norm) %>%
    group_by(racial_appearance) %>%
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    ggplot(aes(racial_appearance, prop, fill = found_norm)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Racial appearance", y = "Proportion", fill = "Found", title = "Proportion found by racial appearance")
}
```

## 4.5 Searches by division / station (if available)

```{r by-division, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
if (has_cols(df, division)) {
  df %>%

    slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    ggplot(aes(reorder(division, n), n)) +
    geom_col() +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(x = "Division", y = "Searches", title = "Top 20 divisions by search volume")
}
```

# 5. Hit-rate summary tables (defensive)

```{r hit-summary}
if (has_cols(df, found_norm)) {
  df %>%
    mutate(found_norm = factor(found_norm)) %>%
    summarise(
      total_searches = n(),
      hits = sum(found_norm == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE),
      hit_rate = hits / total_searches
    ) %>%
    kable(digits = 3, caption = "Overall hit rate") %>%
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
}
```

```{r hit-by-dim}
summarise_hit <- function(.data, dim) {
  if (!all(c(dim, "found_norm") %in% names(.data))) return(NULL)
  .data %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[dim]]), !is.na(found_norm)) %>%
    count(.data[[dim]], found_norm, name = "n") %>%
    group_by(.data[[dim]]) %>%
    mutate(total = sum(n), prop = n / total) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(found_norm == "Yes") %>%
    arrange(desc(prop)) %>%
    rename(dimension = 1) %>%
    select(dimension, hit_rate = prop, total_searches = total)
}

tbls <- list(
  by_age_group = summarise_hit(df, "age_group"),
  by_race      = summarise_hit(df, "racial_appearance"),
  by_division  = summarise_hit(df, "division"),
  by_station   = summarise_hit(df, "station")
)

for (nm in names(tbls)) {
  cat("\n\n###", gsub("_", " ", nm) ,"\n")
  if (!is.null(tbls[[nm]])) {
    print(kable(head(tbls[[nm]], 30), digits = 3, caption = paste("Hit rate —", gsub("_", " ", nm))) %>%
            kable_styling(full_width = FALSE))
  } else {
    cat("_Required columns not found._\n")
  }
}
```

# 6. Data Dictionary (auto + editable)

## 6.1 Auto-generated types

```{r dictionary-auto}
dict_auto <- tibble::tibble(
  column = names(df),
  type = purrr::map_chr(df, ~ class(.x)[1]),
  example = purrr::map_chr(df, ~ as.character(dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(.x)))[1])
)

dict_auto %>%
  kable(caption = "Auto-generated data dictionary (types and first non-missing example)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

## 6.2 Add human‑readable descriptions (fill in the `description` column)

```{r dictionary-editable}
dict_editable <- dict_auto %>%
  mutate(description = "")

dict_editable %>%
  kable(caption = "Editable data dictionary (add your descriptions)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```
